patch_description:
This program performs a targeted crossover between two high-performing ansatz designs:
it combines symmetry-grouped single-qubit rotations and efficient parameter sharing
from the current candidate with motif-aware three-qubit (ZZZ) interactions and
ring-like CRZ entangling structure from the inspiration programs.

Design choices and rationale:
- Preserve parameter budget (13 unique params per block -> 78 total) which was
  associated with good validation/test performance.
- Use lightweight shared RY rotations by symmetry groups (corners/edges/center)
  to capture local variability while keeping parameter count low.
- Entangle the outer ring with a shared CRZ ("crz_ring") to provide global
  circulation-phase coupling reminiscent of a lattice backbone without many unique
  parameters.
- Include separate center-edge CRZ couplings ("crz_center_edge") so the center
  can interact differently with edge qubits.
- Introduce ZZZ motifs placed exactly along the eight winning lines (rows/cols/diags)
  with shared parameters per geometric category (row/col/diag). This encodes
  prior structure potentially important for tic-tac-toe outcomes.
- Add doubly-controlled RZ (CCRZ) center-centered motifs split by geometry
  (edge-edge-center and diag-corner-center) to allow conditional center-phase
  shifts depending on line-like patterns.
- Finish with shared RZ rotations by symmetry group to provide phase flexibility.

All gates respect the connectivity constraints for two-qubit gates; three-qubit
gates (ZZZ, CCRZ) are used only where they are semantically useful (winning lines,
center interactions). Parameter sharing is used deliberately to reduce overfitting
and encourage geometry-aware inductive bias.
